round_robin.implementation: patched kernel/sched/fair.c (pick_next_task_fair / enqueue_task_fair / dequeue_task_fair / task_tick_fair replaced with a linked-list run queue), CFS/EEVDF vruntime logic removed

baseline.note: The original project's README and report call this baseline 'CFS'. That is the traditional name for Linux's fair scheduling class but is not fully accurate for 6.12: Linux transitioned fair-class task selection to EEVDF (pick_eevdf, virtual deadlines) starting in 6.6. The measured data is unaffected; only the baseline's name/description needed correcting. See README.md in this directory.

measured_metrics: perf sched latency (total ms, avg/max delay per task)
top snapshot CPU% distribution across yes processes
limitations: hardware/platform effects (cache, migration, interrupts, I/O stack) are entangled with scheduler-algorithm effects and cannot be separated post hoc
